## Why these topics (and the headline)

GitHub's topic search is the #1 way outsiders find a repo. The list above is
**20 topics, ordered by expected search-traffic weight**:

| Topic | Maps to searches like | Why keep it |
|---|---|---|
| `ai-side-hustle`, `ai-tools`, `revenue` | "ai side hustle", "ai make money" | Anchor topics for the pinned project |
| `data-engineering`, `etl`, `apache-spark`, `kafka`, `flink`, `airflow`, `lakehouse`, `delta-lake` | "spark etl example", "flink cdc" | Breadth = search-engine authority |
| `aws`, `amazon-bedrock` | "aws data project", "bedrock rag" | Cloud credibility |
| `machine-learning`, `llm`, `rag`, `langgraph` | "rag example", "langchain tutorial" | LLM-era search traffic |
| `ai-agents`, `mlops`, `inference` | "ai agent example", "mlops platform" | Niche-but-growing search volume |

The description change matters more than the topics: the previous description
was a topic dump (it read as "I dabble"). The new description leads with one
specific project and what it does, then lists the breadth. A non-technical
visitor now has an entry point; a technical visitor still sees the breadth.

## How to apply this in the GitHub UI

1. Open `https://github.com/vishnoiprem/data-etl-ml/settings` (must be repo owner)
2. Under "General" → "About" → click the gear icon
3. Paste the Description, Website, and Topics strings above
4. Save
5. To pin the repo on your profile: open your profile, click "Customize your pins",
   drag `data-etl-ml` into the pinned grid, save.

After saving, the repo's social preview will look like:
> **vishnoiprem/data-etl-ml**
> An AI side-hustle factory plus 40+ production-style data, ML, RAG, and multi-agent projects. Spark · Kafka · Flink · LangGraph · Bedrock.
